sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Published by Hill (1942) under the name Eutermes perlevis, with the type locality 34 miles south of Darwin, Northern Territory (34 Mile Siding); neither the alate nor the worker is recorded. The soldier is a medium-sized form with a broad head whose sides are distinctly rounded and whose dorsum is slightly convex in lateral view, and a very slender rostrum; it resembles the small E. occultus but is much larger.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A medium-sized species with a broadly rounded head and a very slender rostrum, resembling the small E. occultus but much larger. Head pale orange, paler posteriorly and on the pronotum, rostrum red orange. Head with very few hairs, broad, the sides distinctly rounded, the dorsum slightly convex in lateral view; rostrum about three-fifths as long as the rest of the head, very slender, the anterior three-quarters almost cylindrical (Figs. 206, 207). Antennae short, 12-segmented; segment 2 about half as long as segment 1 and much narrower, the shortest and narrowest of the whole antenna; segment 3 almost as long as segment 1, slender; segments 4—11 slightly shorter than segment 3 and as wide as it; segment 12 almost as long as segment 11, elongate oval. Mandibles without a point. Measurements: total length 4.00; head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.54—1.61; head width 0.99—1.02; pronotum width 0.44.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942). The original uses the old combination Eutermes perlevis, now placed in Australitermes. The original text reads "Winged adult and worker: Not known.", so only the soldier section exists. The type series was taken from a small colony in a nest built by Mirotermes sunteri on the side wall of a large abandoned nest.
